subject: Television & Streaming
title: The West Wing Effect
description: A 60-second lesson on The West Wing Effect.

hook.text: The West Wing presented an idealized White House where smart people argued passionately about policy.

buildup.text: Aaron Sorkin's show made politics look noble.

discovery.text: Studies found the show increased political engagement among viewers.

twist.text: Critics argued The West Wing created a dangerous fantasy—that politics works through good-faith debate.

climax.text: The show demonstrated that fictional politics can inspire real civic participation—but also unrealistic expectations.

punchline.text: A TV fantasy about good government made people want the real thing.

quiz.question: What real-world effect did The West Wing have on its viewers?
options: It increased political engagement and voter participation
